title.en: What a Tank!: the story in brief

text.en: A look at water storage in India and the unique overhead tanks of rural Punjab.

Water conservation has existed for centuries. Hundreds of years ago huge water storage structures stored water, protected cities from floods, gave drinking water and brought people together.
Many communities still use traditional methods. In Tamil Nadu, Ooranis store rainwater for drinking and farming. In Kerala, Panam Keni wells do not dry up even in the hottest months. In Rajasthan's Thar region, Tankas are underground tanks that can store water for six to seven months.
Today most homes have tanks, often on the roof, called overhead water tanks.
In rural Punjab, in the north-west of India, the overhead tanks have unique designs. You may see tanks shaped like a giant flower, a football, a brown rooster, a statue or an aeroplane.
The tank tells us about the people of the house. A farmer may have a tractor, bullock cart or rooster tank. A football lover may have a football tank.
The tanks are made of cement. A frame of steel rods is made first, then concrete gives the final shape, and the tank is installed on the roof. It holds hundreds of litres.
These unique water tanks are the heart of the communities in rural Punjab.
